a: Every data-bearing element is a re-executable `DataBinding` to a governed Superset query, not a copy of numbers. It does not mean real-time streaming or a PPTX that queries Superset by itself.

q: How does the GCK run protocol work and what endpoints does it have?
a: A run is a background task in the engine; HTTP connections only observe it. Six endpoints: `POST /v1/runs`, `GET .../events` (the stream), `GET /v1/runs/{runId}`, `GET .../artifact`, `POST .../input` (outline decision) and `POST .../cancel`. A dropped connection never restarts generation; only cancel stops it. Data uses `/v1/data/catalog`, `/v1/data/resolve` and `/v1/render`.

q: Which events does a GCK run stream to the browser?
a: Each SSE frame carries one event in a versioned envelope: `run.started`, `plan.proposed`, `run.awaiting_input`, `artifact.patch` (RFC 6902 JSON Patch, the main content channel), optional `text.delta`, `binding.resolved` per data binding, `run.warning`, and terminal `run.completed` or `run.failed`. Event ids are gapless so the client can resume.

q: Why does GCK use fetch-based SSE instead of EventSource, and how does resume work?
a: `EventSource` cannot POST or send an `Authorization` header, so `@gck/client` reads SSE through fetch. The engine keeps each run as an event log; on reconnect the client sends `Last-Event-ID` and receives only later events. The engine writes a heartbeat every 15 seconds and the client reconnects after 45 seconds of silence.

a: `createRegistry()` maps an id or alias to an adapter and refuses invalid manifests (`checkManifest`), duplicates and missing `serialize`, `validateNative` or `deserialize` at registration. Its `convert(udm, targetId)` always runs `negotiate` before `serialize` and returns native output plus all losses. Only one setup file imports adapters, so the core never names a target.

q: How do capability negotiation and the degradation chain work?
a: Core `negotiate(udm, manifest)` reduces a UDM to what the manifest supports, in one fixed order for every target: ext bags, notes, section titles, blocks (chains such as chart to table to list to paragraph), chart kinds, marks, nesting, structure, limits. Each change becomes a loss entry such as `ext_dropped` or `block_degraded`; adapters never degrade content themselves.

q: How does the Tiptap adapter negotiate with the host editor's schema?
a: The adapter never assumes extensions. `createTiptapAdapter` builds the schema with `getSchema(extensions)` (no DOM) and `deriveManifest(schema, id)` lists only blocks and marks that schema has: tables need the table nodes, charts need `dataBlock`, and ids, ext pass-through, callouts and patch need `udmAttrs`. A StarterKit-only editor yields the lossier `tiptap.basic` profile.

q: Which custom Tiptap nodes does the adapter add (dataBlock, udmAttrs)?
a: Two: one generic `dataBlock` atom for charts, diagrams, metrics, live tables and embeds (attributes `kind`, `bindingId`, `block`, `binding`), replacing Part IX's one node per kind; and `udmAttrs`, which adds global `udmId`, `udmGroup`, `udmRole`, `udmKind`, `udmMeta` and `udmExt` to top-level nodes so ids and slot provenance survive editing. Splitting a paragraph duplicates its id.

q: How is Tiptap output validated?
a: `validateNative` runs three layers: `schema.nodeFromJSON` rejects unknown nodes, marks and empty text; `check()` rejects invalid content such as text directly in `doc`; a diff of `toJSON()` against the input catches attributes Tiptap silently dropped or changed, plus a heading-level range check. Seven negative controls were rejected, and output passed for 383/383 layouts.

q: How does the Presenton adapter write back (patch vs content mode)?
a: Per section. Patch mode, when `ext` links to an existing slide: copy its current `ui` and rewrite only changed slots (provenance slot first, then shape, then position). Content mode, for new sections: structure LLM step picks a layout (capacity-checked, deterministic fallback), then content JSON is hydrated. Smart patch for Smart HTML slides. A patch guard blocks geometry or style changes.

q: What are extension fields (`ext`) in the UDM?
aliases: slot path layout id in ext
a: `ext` is the only place target data may live: one bag per adapter-id namespace on the document, sections and blocks (never text segments). An adapter writes only `ext[manifest.id]`; pass-through adapters carry foreign bags unchanged, others drop them with `ext_dropped`. The engine never interprets it, the LLM never writes it, removing it must not change meaning, and size caps are proposed.

q: How is live data handled in the UDM and the Tiptap page?
a: Part IX's rule holds: blocks reference bindings by key, the UDM stores definitions only, values resolve as the viewer from the binding store, and numbers enter prose only as tokens. Imported charts and typed tables use a new `static` source holding a snapshot. Tiptap's `dataBlock.attrs.binding` keeps only the definition (the production node rejects runtime fields). Live tokens were not prototyped.
